newsitem.title: USA: P&G asks $101 mln damages in Paragon dispute.
newsitem.headline: P&G asks $101 mln damages in Paragon dispute.

text.p: In the first day of the trial of a major patent dispute, Procter & Gamble Co attorney John Sweeney said the company would seek damages and interest of $101 million from rival Paragon Trade Brands Inc.
In January 1994 P&G sued Paragon for allegedly infringing two P&G patents for improving the fit and comfort of disposable diapers.

Sweeney told Judge Joseph Longobardi of the U.S. District Court in Delaware that the damages include $60 million for lost P&G profits based on eight percent of Paragon's sales from March 1991 through December 1994.

P&G also wants a 2-1/2 percent royalty or $30 million on Paragon's remaining sales in the same 46 month period. That would translate to approximately $325 million in annual sales for Paragon. Sweeney said he will ask that any damages awarded be tripled for alleged willful infringement.

But Paragon attorney Stephen Judlowe told Longobardi "(Our) position is this patent is invalid. The reality is we don't use it anymore." He called the lawsuit P&G's "last gasp to keep this product from becoming a commodity" and to keep Paragon from a larger share of the market.
He said P&G's demand a year ago of $472 million in damages had been repeatedly lowered and the royalty rate reduced from five percent to 2-1/2 percent.

"Profit margins are five to six percent...Licenses signed when patents go to trial mean nothing," Judlowe said because the licensee ends up paying either a low royalty if the patent is upheld or no royalty if the patent is declared invalid.
Also at issue in this trial is Paragon's countersuit against P&G. Paragon seeks damages of about $5 million from P&G for alleged infringement of Paragon's patent for a "low-bulk disposable" diaper.

P&G associate general counsel Patrick Lane told Reuters Kimberly-Clark Corp, which makes Huggies diapers and has a cross licensing agreement with P&G, has a similar patent suit pending against Paragon in Dallas. Kimberly-Clark officials were in court today to observe the trial, Lane said.

Together, P&G and Kimberly-Clark control 72 percent of the U.S. diaper market, according to P&G's Steward. But Judlowe told Judge Longobardi that "Customers walk past Huggies, Pampers and Luvs for something cheaper."
P&G, of Cincinnati, Ohio, sells disposable diapers under the trade names "Pampers" and "Luvs."
Paragon is a private-label diaper maker based in Norcross, Georgia near Atlanta.
The non-jury trial is scheduled for three weeks.
